source: Editorial selection, 2026-09-03. San Francisco has no single canonical neighborhood list and this roster does not pretend otherwise: SF Planning publishes 41 Analysis Neighborhoods, DataSF's SF Find layer carries 117, and neither matches the units a visitor uses. Twenty neighborhoods were chosen for visitor material, plus three pages for places that are not neighborhoods at all. The declined candidates are recorded below with reasons so the narrowing is answerable rather than invisible.
scope_ruling: Twenty neighborhoods plus three standalone park pages. The Presidio is federal land under the National Park Service and the city does not administer it; Golden Gate Park touches the Richmond, the Sunset and Haight-Ashbury alike; Ocean Beach is GGNRA. Folding any of them into a neighborhood would assert a containment that is false, so each is claimed by nobody and the marquee gate holds it at exactly one file. This is the Rome precedent: Forest Park, Alley Pond Park and Flushing Meadows Corona Park were each ruled to belong to no neighborhood and shipped as their own pages.
designation_ruling: UNLIKE ROME, designation claims PUBLISH — with a citation. Rome banned every protection claim because Vincoli in Rete and the Catalogo generale were both unreachable, so no claim could be checked. San Francisco's registers answered during scoping on 2026-09-03: the DataSF Socrata API, SF Planning and the National Register all returned HTTP 200, and the two landmark dataset IDs that returned 404 are wrong resource identifiers rather than a dead host. So a designation claim must name its register and its identifier — an Article 10 landmark number, or an NRHP reference number — and the gate asserts the citation is present rather than forbidding the claim. A claim with no identifier does not publish.
photo_ruling: The United States has freedom of panorama for BUILDINGS under 17 USC 120(a), so a Commons file under CC0, PD, CC BY or CC BY-SA showing a building from public land publishes — the rule the Bronx and Queens ran on, and not Rome's four-gate rule, which existed because Italy has no freedom of panorama at all. THE REFINEMENT IS NOT OPTIONAL: 120(a) covers architectural works and does NOT cover sculptures, murals or other public artworks, which keep full copyright. San Francisco is dense with them. A photograph whose framing FEATURES a public artwork still needs its artist and death year established; a building does not. Known cases: Cupid's Span on the Embarcadero (Claes Oldenburg d. 2022, Coosje van Bruggen d. 2009), the Vaillancourt Fountain (Armand Vaillancourt, living), and the Mission murals of Balmy Alley and Clarion Alley.
kind_note: A place's kind must be one of the thirteen the schema allows: museum, theater, restaurant, cafe, brewery, hotel, bnb, park, historic-site, amusement-park, shop, stadium, attraction. There is NO church, monument, square or bridge kind. Rome shipped three places with an invented kind and the changeset rejected them at seed time; Ethos.Seeds.SanFranciscoSeedDataTest reads the list off Ethos.Places.Place.kinds/0 rather than a copy, so the two cannot drift.
oracle_park_ruling: Ethos.Seeds.OracleParkPlaces is a live code seed already owning seven places with town "San Francisco": oracle-park, reds-java-house, momos-san-francisco, flour-and-water-pizza-shop-mission-rock, arsicault-bakery-mission-rock, blue-bottle-coffee-mission-rock and china-basin-park. Mission Bay LINKS to guide:oracle-park-guide and restates none of them, the way Concourse links to Yankee Stadium and Flushing to Citi Field. That makes seed_ballparks/1 a genuine precondition of the San Francisco seeder, because Links.resolve!/1 raises on an unknown target and aborts a run that is not transactional.
destination_slug_ruling: Guide.derive_destination_slug/1 takes only the FIRST comma-segment of the destination string and discards the state, so "Chinatown, California" and "Chinatown, New York" both derive `chinatown` and would co-list on one destination page. Measured against the 336 destination slugs already committed, exactly three of these twenty-three collide, all with Manhattan: Chinatown, Financial District and Union Square. Each is resolved by changing the DESTINATION STRING so the first segment differs, which is what the Queens gate documents, and never by weakening the assertion. Co-listing remains possible where it is wanted: Flushing and Citi Field share one destination page deliberately, which is why the assertion excludes code-seed guides.

zones.name: Mission District
zones.draw: Mission Dolores, the murals of Balmy Alley and Clarion Alley, Dolores Park, Valencia and 24th Streets. NOTE the murals are ARTWORKS, not buildings, so the photo refinement applies.

zones.name: North Beach
zones.draw: Washington Square, Saints Peter and Paul Church, City Lights Booksellers, Coit Tower and Telegraph Hill, the Italian cafes of Columbus Avenue.

zones.name: Chinatown
zones.draw: The Dragon Gate at Grant and Bush, Waverly Place, Tin How Temple, the Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Factory, Portsmouth Square. DESTINATION STRING DISAMBIGUATED from Manhattan's Chinatown.

zones.name: Haight-Ashbury
zones.draw: The Haight and Ashbury intersection, the Victorians of Ashbury Heights, Amoeba Music, Buena Vista Park, the Grateful Dead house at 710 Ashbury.

zones.name: The Castro
zones.draw: The Castro Theatre, Harvey Milk's camera shop at 575 Castro, the Rainbow Honor Walk, Pink Triangle Park, Corona Heights.

zones.name: Marina District
zones.draw: The Palace of Fine Arts, Fort Mason, Chestnut Street, Marina Green, the Wave Organ. NOTE Crissy Field and the Presidio proper are the Presidio's, not the Marina's.

zones.name: SoMa
zones.draw: SFMOMA, Yerba Buena Gardens, the Contemporary Jewish Museum, the Museum of the African Diaspora, South Park. Boundaries are genuinely contested; the arbitration barrier exists for this.

zones.name: Fisherman's Wharf
zones.draw: Pier 39 and the sea lions, the Hyde Street Pier historic ships, Ghirardelli Square, the Musee Mecanique, Aquatic Park.

zones.name: Nob Hill
zones.draw: Grace Cathedral, Huntington Park, the Fairmont and Mark Hopkins hotels, the Cable Car Museum, the Pacific-Union Club.

zones.name: Russian Hill
zones.draw: The Lombard Street crooked block, Macondray Lane, the Vallejo Street steps, San Francisco Art Institute, Ina Coolbrith Park.

zones.name: Pacific Heights
zones.draw: The Haas-Lilienthal House, Lafayette Park, Alta Plaza Park, Fillmore Street, the Spreckels Mansion.

zones.name: Hayes Valley
zones.draw: Patricia's Green, the War Memorial Opera House and Davies Symphony Hall edge, Hayes Street shops, the Proxy project.

zones.name: Japantown
zones.draw: The Peace Pagoda and Peace Plaza, the Japan Center malls, Buchanan Street Mall, the Sundance Kabuki, Konko Church.

zones.name: Financial District
zones.draw: The Transamerica Pyramid, the Ferry Building, Jackson Square, the Wells Fargo History Museum, Embarcadero Plaza. DESTINATION STRING DISAMBIGUATED from Manhattan's Financial District.

zones.name: Union Square
zones.draw: The square itself and the Dewey Monument, Maiden Lane, the Westin St. Francis, the cable car turntable at Powell and Market. DESTINATION STRING DISAMBIGUATED from Manhattan's Union Square.

zones.name: Inner Richmond
zones.draw: Clement Street, the Columbarium, Temple Emanu-El, Presidio Heights edge, the Green Apple Books block.

zones.name: Inner Sunset
zones.draw: Irving Street, Mount Sutro, the UCSF Parnassus campus, the 9th and Irving block. NOTE the de Young and the Academy of Sciences are IN Golden Gate Park, which is its own page.

zones.name: Dogpatch
zones.draw: The Minnesota Street Project, Museum of Craft and Design, the Pier 70 historic yard, Esprit Park, the surviving workers' cottages.

zones.name: Mission Bay
zones.draw: Chase Center, the UCSF Mission Bay campus, Mission Creek and the houseboats. ORACLE PARK AND ITS SEVEN PLACES ARE A CODE SEED — link to guide:oracle-park-guide and restate none of them.

zones.name: Noe Valley
zones.draw: 24th Street, the Noe Valley Town Square, Billy Goat Hill, the Victorians of Liberty Hill.

zones.name: The Presidio
zones.draw: Crissy Field, the Walt Disney Family Museum, Fort Point under the bridge, the Presidio Officers' Club, the National Cemetery, Andy Goldsworthy's Spire and Wood Line. NOTE the Goldsworthy pieces are ARTWORKS and he is living: photo refinement applies. Claimed by no neighborhood — federal land the city does not administer.

zones.name: Golden Gate Park
zones.draw: The de Young Museum, the California Academy of Sciences, the Japanese Tea Garden, the Conservatory of Flowers, Stow Lake, the Botanical Garden. Claimed by no neighborhood — it touches the Richmond, the Sunset and Haight-Ashbury alike.

zones.name: Ocean Beach
zones.draw: The beach itself, the Cliff House site, Sutro Baths ruins, Lands End trail, the Camera Obscura. Claimed by no neighborhood — GGNRA land.

declined.name: Telegraph Hill
declined.reason: Absorbed by North Beach in most sources, and Coit Tower is North Beach's marquee. A straddle the arbitration barrier settles rather than a page.

declined.name: The Embarcadero
declined.reason: Absorbed by the Financial District and Fisherman's Wharf. It is a waterfront road rather than a neighborhood, and the Ferry Building already anchors the Financial District page.

declined.name: Outer Sunset
declined.reason: Twenty was the number chosen. Its principal visitor draw is Ocean Beach, which has its own page.

declined.name: Bernal Heights
declined.reason: Twenty was the number chosen. Strong candidate for a later wave; Bernal Hill and Cortland Avenue would carry a page.

declined.name: Potrero Hill
declined.reason: Twenty was the number chosen. Adjacent to Dogpatch, which took the industrial-heritage material.

declined.name: Alamo Square
declined.reason: Twenty was the number chosen. The Painted Ladies are its single draw and sit at the edge of Hayes Valley's reach.

declined.name: Twin Peaks
declined.reason: Twenty was the number chosen. A viewpoint rather than a neighborhood, and closer in kind to the three park pages than to the twenty.
